stories.title: Community in 'shock' following multi-victim Dublin crash
stories.summary: The local community is "shocked and devastated" following the crash in south Dublin yesterday in which six teenagers and a woman in her 40s were injured, a local councillor for Dún Laoghaire has said. A car mounted a footpath outside a row of shops on Oliver Plunkett Road in Monkstown Farm, Dún Laoghaire, at around 3pm. Three girls and three boys, aged between 13 and 15, were brought to CHI Temple Street and CHI Crumlin to be treated for a range of injuries, some described as critical. There have been reports the driver suffered a medical episode and lost control of the car, which then mounted the pavement. Another 15-year-old boy who witnessed the scene was taken to CHI Tallaght for medical attention. Fine Gael Councillor Lorraine Hall said the teenagers had been standing on a footpath on a nice evening, which made the incident all the more shocking.

stories.title: Western railway platform extensions expected next year
stories.summary: Extensions of railway station platforms between Limerick and Athenry in Co Galway are expected to be completed by the end of the next year, as part of an effort to boost passenger capacity on the route. Iarnród Éireann is issuing tender documents for the construction works at five stations today. This will allow for six carriage trains to stop at Sixmilebridge, Ennis, Gort, Ardrahan and Craughwell. Platforms will be extended by 55 metres at four of the stations, with a 12 metre enhancement planned for Ennis. Iarnród Éireann said track enabling works are already under way and that it hopes to award a contract to the successful applicant by the end of the year. Chief Executive Mary Considine said the initiative will increase capacity and broaden transport options for those living close to the Galway - Limerick rail line.

stories.title: Derry not resting with work to be done ahead of 2027
stories.summary: Derry City claimed a seventh Club Orange Men's FAI Cup since 1985 yesterday. That's two more than any other club in that time period. Questions will now centre around whether the Candystripes can drive on and finally reach their potential, and the league crown that supporters so desperately crave. And while celebrations are in full swing in the north-west, immediate concern at the Ryan McBride Brandywell Stadium will turn to the question of who will be managing the club at the start of the 2027 season. The last time the club were in the cup final, Ruaidhrí Higgins left the club after Drogheda United upset them. Tiernan Lynch replaced him, but his reign came to an end this summer. Mark Connolly, appointed two months earlier as the Head of Football at the club, was thrust into the manager's job on an interim basis. "I think this went all right," he said at yesterday's post-match press conference.

stories.title: Sixth couple eliminated from Strictly Come Dancing
stories.summary: Bethany Antonia and Nancy Xu have become the sixth couple to be eliminated from Strictly Come Dancing after being defeated in the dance off. On the results show, the couple reprised their foxtrot to Bleeding Love by Leona Lewis, which had scored them 30 on Saturday’s live show, putting them joint fourth in the leaderboard before public votes were taken into account. They faced former Love Island contestant Cach Mercer and his partner Maddie Ingoldsby, who performed their waltz to That Ain’t You by Mulaa Joans, which scored 26, putting them joint bottom of the leaderboard on judge’s scores. After both couples danced, judge Anton Du Beke chose to save Mercer and Ingoldsby, while fellow judges Motsi Mabuse and Craig Revel Horwood voted to save Antonia and Xu, head judge Shirley Ballas had Sunday’s deciding vote and saved Mercer and Ingoldsby. It comes after the show saw former Love Island winner Dani Dyer top the leaderboard with her partner Nikita Kuzmin, getting their first 10 as they scored 36 for their American smooth to It Had to Be You by Harry Connick Jr. The results show also commemorated Britain's Remembrance Sunday with a group performance from the Strictly professionals.

stories.title: Winners of the 2026 Food & Wine Restaurant of the Year Awards
stories.summary: The 2026 Food&Wine Restaurant of the Year Awards took place last night, celebrating the best of Ireland's hospitality industry. From neighbourhood gems to destination dining, the awards honour outstanding food, service, creativity and consistency across the country. This year's panel of judges consisted of a wide range of journalists and industry experts, including Ali Dunworth, Aoife Carrigy, Bairbre Power, Cathal McBride, Gillian Nelis, Joanne Cronin, Marcus O'Laoire, and the late Corinna Hardgrave, an esteemed restaurant critic who passed away this past October. This year's ceremony saw Artie Clifford of Blas na hÉireann inducted into the Food&Wine Restaurant of the Year Hall of Fame for 2026. The most notable award of the night, 'Restaurant of the Year', went to The Lady Helen at Mount Juliet. The Michelin-starred restaurant is one of Ireland's most unique dining experiences, serving modern cuisine in a 260-year-old country manor, under the guidance of Chef John Kelly. The venue also took home the title of 'Pastry Chef of the Year' thanks to Tom Phelan, who just wrapped nine years of service at the restaurant, as well as 'Best Restaurant — Leinster 2026' and 'Best Chef — Leinster 2026', which went to Chef John Kelly.

stories.title: Sides to discuss 'improved' 10.5% public sector pay offer
stories.summary: Trade unions and Government representatives will continue engagement today with an independent group in a bid to find a pathway to talks on the ongoing pay dispute. Over the weekend the Government made what it described as a "substantially improved" pay offer. It is understood the revised pay offer would deliver pay increases of 10.5% in an agreement that would run until the early months of 2029. This would equate to an 11% uplift when the increases are compounded over the duration of the agreement. There would be a bigger package and increases for lower paid public servants, with some benefitting by up to 17.8%. stories.title: Kingspan retains full year profit guidance for 2026
stories.summary: Insulation and building company Kingspan has today retained its full year profit guidance for 2026, adding that its pipeline continues to develop very positively. In a trading update in the period up to the end of September, Kingspan said that sales in the nine‐month period to the end of September rose by 10% to €7.6 billion from the same time last year. Sales were up 16% in the third quarter mainly due to strong underlying sales growth of 12%, it added. Co-Cavan based Kingspan said that while its end-markets have their obvious challenges the global backlog is ahead year on year, adding that there is still some way to go in the current year with much of the seasonally important fourth quarter remaining. "We continue to expect to deliver a full year trading profit in the region of €1,150m for the current year +20% versus 2025. Assuming our end-markets remain relatively stable, the strong backlog and pipeline ought to support a trading profit in the region of €1,470m in 202," it added. Kingspan said sales at its Insulated Building Envelopes sales rose by 4% in the first nine months and by 8% in the third quarter.

stories.title: Pride for Connolly after tumultuous year ends with cup
stories.summary: Derry City interim manager Mark Connolly was delighted to see his side finish a challenging season on a high by claiming the Club Orange Men's FAI Cup. The Candystripes were 1-0 winners over Waterford at Aviva Stadium, with Darragh Burns getting the only goal of an edgy contest. Connolly returned to the Brandywell in June as the Director of Football but found himself in the hotseat after the dismissal of Tiernan Lynch in early August. From there, Derry were able to turn things around, with their cup success securing lucrative European soccer for next summer. For Connolly, it was a satisfying conclusion to a tough few months in the job. "It's been a tough number of months for myself coming back into the club. Just trying to get stuff back in place and trying to get the good times back, get the city back on side.

stories.summary: UN chief Antonio Guterres has urged world leaders to "get serious" about tackling climate change as the COP31 conference was set to open with negotiators already tangled in an early fight over money. The UN General Secretary made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish city of Antalya for the UN's annual climate talks. The summit comes after a year of punishing heatwaves in Europe, major wildfires in Indonesia and catastrophic floods in Nepal, with an exceptionally strong El Niño weather phenomenon fuelling more climate chaos. "We have entered a new age of climate extremes," mR Guterres said in a statement. He urged leaders to "get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need". But the COP31 opening ceremony was delayed by an hour without explanation.

stories.title: How often should you be working at the office?
stories.summary: Analysis: While there's no single magic number, evidence suggests two to three days days in the office – and on the same days as your colleagues Office attendance from Monday to Friday used to be a pretty standard requirement for many jobs, but plenty of employees have now developed a taste for working from home. In response, some of their employers have started to tighten the rules on hybrid work. Barclays Bank is one of latest big companies to do so, telling thousands of staff they must be in the office at least three days a week instead of two. So what is the right balance for those who split the locations of their working week? Plenty of research has now been done on that question. And while it does not give a single magic number, the evidence does suggest that the best range is two or three days in the office – on the same days as your colleagues. For example, in a study involving a large online travel agency in China, more than 1,500 engineers, marketing and finance staff were allowed to work from home on Wednesdays and Fridays, while a control group stayed in the office full time. Over the following two years of performance reviews, the performance of the hybrid workers was equal in quality to those who stayed in the office. Those who worked from home were much less likely to leave the company – especially women and the workers with long commutes. A smaller experiment at an international development organisation went a step further, by randomly varying how many days 148 staff spent in the office. Those who came in around two days a week said they had a better work-life balance, more job satisfaction and less isolation than colleagues who came in more or less often. Their performance was unaffected.

stories.summary: Rivals actor Alex Hassell has said a scene which sees him caught playing nude tennis was "really important" for the Disney+ series. The scene saw the 46-year-old's character Rupert Campbell-Black and Emily Atack’s character Sarah Stratton playing tennis naked when Taggie O’Hara, played by Bella Maclean, walks in on them to warn of a fire. Speaking to The Telegraph, Hassell said: "I feel that the full-frontal stuff was really important, also, it’s funny and shocking, and I think it’s memorable in a way that is helpful now in the latter part of the story. "But I think, also, it’s diminishing returns. If we’re seeing my willy all the time, I think it’ll make less of an impression." The scene was nominated for the 2025 Bafta Memorable Moment award, which was eventually won by Chris McCausland and Dianne Buswell’s waltz to You’ll Never Walk Alone on Strictly Come Dancing. The second part of the second season of Rivals is set to air on the streaming platform on November 11 and will reportedly see the actor, who said he is "not shy about my body", go nude again.

stories.summary: Nvidia has said its board was probing whether CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, after a media report alleged he had a close relationship with a ⁠Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Mr Huang said in a message to employees that he had been "unfaithful" to his wife and took "full responsibility" for his actions, while Nvidia said the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company without interruption. The developments are likely to pressure the chipmaker's stock, which has already fallen sharply amid worries about the AI boom's sustainability, and may also raise questions about his future at the helm of the company he co-founded, analysts said. The New York Times reported last month that Mr Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. Mr Huang admitted to having been unfaithful to his wife, saying, "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I ⁠did. I am deeply sorry." Addressing his colleagues, board, partners and shareholders, he said: "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. stories.title: Fuel prices dip in November, but EV charging costs rise
stories.summary: New figures show a small fall in the price of petrol and diesel at the pumps in November, while public EV charging costs rose. AA Ireland's latest fuel price analysis shows that petrol averaged €1.96 per litre in November, down 2.26 cents from October's average of €1.98, a decrease of about 1%. Diesel averaged €2.13 per litre, down 1.87 cents from €2.15 in October, a decrease of around 1%. AA Ireland said the November averages equate to approximately €78.36 for a 40 litre petrol fill and €106.45 for a 50 litre diesel fill. AA Ireland said that pump prices are influenced by a range of international factors, including global oil prices, wholesale fuel costs, geopolitical developments and currency movements. Changes in these underlying costs can feed through to the prices motorists ultimately pay at the pump.

stories.title: Trump 'only kidding' over press role offer to UFC boss
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has said he was only joking when he offered the role of White House press secretary to Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White at the weekend. "I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Mr Trump told reporters on the tarmac of his namesake airport in Florida. The press secretary role - traditionally one of the administration's most visible positions - has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on 16 October after less than a week on the job. Mr White, the 57-year-old president and CEO of UFC, is a long-time friend of the president. Speaking in London late Saturday, Mr White was reticent, saying that he would "have more to talk about" after meeting with Mr Trump today. Mr White's UFC staged a bloody cage fight on the White House South Lawn on Mr Trump's 80th birthday in June, and he appeared on stage with Mr Trump during his re-election victory speech in 2024.

stories.title: Top-10 finish for Power in Mexico as Brown wins play-off
stories.summary: Séamus Power enjoyed a strong finish to the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico to finish tied for eighth, five shots behind tournament winner Blades Brown. At 19 years, five months and 18 days old, Brown is nearly six months younger than Jordan Spieth was when the three-time major champion claimed his first win at the 2013 John Deere Classic, the last time the tour had a teenage winner. Power, who had excelled in Saturday's third round with a 65, almost matched that in Sunday's closing round. The Waterford man carded a six-under 66 to finish the tournament on 18 under. Power got off on the wrong foot with a bogey on the first. But things would only get better from there on the El Cardonal at Diamante course at Cabo San Lucas. A birdie on the third had him pointing in the right direction and three holes later, an eagle on the par-5 sixth had him two under for the day.

stories.title: The cautionary tale of the disappearing town
stories.summary: As world leaders gather in Turkey for COP31 this week, support for countries hardest hit by climate change will be high on the agenda. Among those nations is Honduras, where extreme weather and rising sea levels are increasingly threatening communities. Reporter Kate Varley and cameraman Bram Verbeke travelled to the Central American country to hear from those on the frontlines of the crisis. When you ask the people of Cedeño to describe the town they've called home for decades, one word comes up time and again: paradise. Nestled between sandy beaches and lush forests, this community on Honduras' Pacific coast looks like it belongs on a glossy postcard. Cedeño is fighting for its survival, and month by month it is losing a battle to the advancing sea - turning what was once a slice of paradise into a source of despair for residents.

stories.summary: Liam Scales provided a looping finish to earn Celtic a 1-0 victory over Kilmarnock. The Republic of Ireland defender hooked a Camilo Duran cross into the top corner in the 26th minute to restore Celtic's four-point lead in the Scottish Premiership. Celtic – and Kasper Hogh in particular – otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty. Hogh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without a goal hit the 16-game mark since he netted a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance. The Danish striker finished from seven yards after being set up by Nygren and ran to the standing section to celebrate. His joy was short-lived as referee John Beaton was summoned to the monitor and gave a free-kick to Killie for Mika Baur’s challenge on Greg Kiltie.

stories.title: Krakow shooting suspect dies in hospital, say police
stories.summary: The alleged perpetrator of a deadly weekend shooting spree in Krakow has died, Polish police said, two days after he was critically wounded in a shootout with officers. "We inform you that the perpetrator of the tragic events died this morning in the hospital," regional police said in a post on X of the 24-year-old Polish man who allegedly opened fire on Saturday in central Krakow, killing six people. Authorities said the man had been "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the shooting - the deadliest in the country since the end of communism in 1989 - an act of "terrorism". Six people, including two foreigners, were killed in the shooting spree, and about 15 others were wounded, according to authorities. The gunman is suspected to have killed nine people in total after the bodies of three people - his parents and sister - were found at their home two hours' drive from Krakow. Meanwhile, Poland is facing a week of political tensions after the shooting shattered residents' sense of security in the deeply divided nation.

The Republic of Ireland striker was unable to get on the scoresheet himself in his 78 minutes on the pitch. Parrott did have one half-chance in the 17th minute with a swivel and strike at goal that went just wide of the near post, while another effort from outside the box also deflected the other side of that post early in the second half. But goals in the last ten minutes of normal time from Rodrigo Riquelme and Marc Bartra ultimately proved enough for Betis to get past third-from-bottom Elche.

stories.title: Russell Brand to be sentenced for rape and assaults
stories.summary: British comedian and actor Russell Brand is set to return to court today to be sentenced for raping a young woman and sexually assaulting three other women. Brand, 51, was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court in London of raping a woman in 2009, as well as sexually assaulting female TV and radio workers between 2004 and 2009. Mr Justice Bennathan ordered Brand to start his prison sentence immediately after being found guilty last Thursday afternoon. The judge is expected to hear impact statements from Brand's victims and legal submissions from lawyers before passing sentence. A four-week trial heard how Brand preyed on women who he encountered on his way to becoming one of Britain’s best-known comedians, TV and radio hosts and actors. He claimed to have only ever had consensual sex during a "promiscuous" life, which he insisted had been packed with "idiocy" but never illegal.

stories.title: Man Utd claw back draw with stoppage-time goals v Villa
stories.summary: Patrick Dorgu secured Manchester United a scarcely believable 4-4 draw deep into stoppage time as under-fire Michael Carrick denied Aston Villa amid a backdrop of anger against the club's ownership. Old Trafford witnessed an astonishing helter-skelter encounter on Sunday afternoon as the embattled, and deeply flawed, Red Devils showed spirit against the odds as they had against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday. United again fell two goals behind as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson capitalised on wretched play inside four minutes as supporters called for the Glazers and United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to sell up. Bruno Fernandes pulled one back from the spot, just like in the 3-2 Champions League comeback victory against Roma, and Youri Tielemans equalised against his former club just before half-time. But renewed United hope was dented at the start of the second half, with John McGinn scoring a penalty gifted to Villa by Diogo Dalot – whose substitution would be brutally cheered – before Leon Goretzka added another. They were the latest self-inflicted wounds in a season of gaffes by Carrick’s side but the players fought until the death, with substitute Joshua Zirkzee reducing the deficit in stoppage time before fellow substitute Dorgu sparked bedlam.

stories.title: Commission seeks information on sexual abuse in schools
stories.summary: The Commission of Investigation examining the handling of historical child sexual abuse in schools has called on members of the public here and abroad to come forward with any information that could help its work. A survey launched by the commission last month has received hundreds of responses, but the team is keen to hear from others before it closes on 7 December. New information has emerged in relation to schools that were not previously examined, which is why the commission is appealing for more people to take the survey. The Commission of Investigation's remit relates to the handling of concerns relating to child sexual abuse in all schools between 1927 and 2013. It was established after a Scoping Inquiry into day and boarding schools run by religious orders revealed widespread historical abuse. The commission's work is much wider than the Scoping Inquiry. As a statutory body, it holds far more power, enabling it, for example, to compel witnesses and documentation.

stories.title: Magnificent seven for Derry as Burns sinks Waterford
stories.summary: Derry City further enhanced their reputation as cup specialists with a 1-0 victory over Waterford in the Club Orange Men's FAI Cup final this afternoon at Aviva Stadium. Darragh Burns got the only goal of the game with a fine strike from the edge of the box midway through the second half to secure a seventh cup triumph for the Candystripes since joining the League of Ireland in 1985. For the Blues, it's another defeat in the decider, 22 years after their last one, with their 46-year wait for a victory set to go on for another season, at least. A crowd of 36,093 paid in to watch a stop-start decider, which the Blues shaded for a good chunk of the middle of the game, but Derry showed that little bit of ruthlessness to get over the line. While the Ulstermen had finished two places higher in the League of Ireland, Waterford had been in better form coming into the game, having also recorded a more recent victory in clashes between the sides. But it's Derry who will be heading for Europe next summer, not before the celebrations kick into gear this evening; their league disappointment and the James McClean saga now long behind them.

stories.title: Seven injured as car mounts footpath in south Dublin
stories.summary: Six teenage pedestrians and a woman in her 40s have been injured after the car she was driving mounted a footpath outside a row of shops in south Dublin. Three boys and three girls were taken to CHI Temple Street and CHI Crumlin to be treated for a range of injuries, some described as critical. The driver of the car remains in hospital for medical attention. Gardaí had initially said seven pedestrians had been involved in the collision. Another 15-year-old boy who witnessed the scene was taken to CHI Tallaght for medical attention. Gardaí and other emergency services were called to the scene on the Oliver Plunkett Road, near the junction with Kill Avenue, in Monkstown Farm, Dún Laoghaire at around 3pm yesterday.

stories.title: Two arrested on suspicion of murder of Limerick woman
stories.summary: A further two people have been arrested on suspicion of the murder of Limerick woman Carrie Mullane, who went missing after travelling to Co Fermanagh last month. The PSNI believes the 39-year-old mother of four was killed shortly after arriving in Enniskillen and have been searching for her body since being made aware of her disappearance on 29 October. Detectives investigating her disappearance arrested a woman aged in her 60s and a man aged in his 30s in Enniskillen on suspicion of murder. A 35-year-old man appeared in court yesterday charged with murder and preventing the lawful burial of a corpse. Police divers have been searching for Ms Mullane's body in an area of Upper Lough Erne just outside Enniskillen for a number of days. Detective Superintendent Richard Thornton said the investigation into locating Ms Mullane is ongoing.

stories.title: Tánaiste 'would like' apology over Thalidomide in 2026
stories.summary: Tánaiste Simon Harris has said he stands over his comments that 2026 has to be the year when the Government finally resolves the outstanding issues facing thalidomide survivors, including a State apology. Thalidomide was prescribed to pregnant mothers in the 1950s and 1960s as an anti-morning sickness drug, but was later withdrawn because of links to birth defects and lifelong disabilities. The German manufacturer apologised in 2012 to those born without limbs as a result of its use. Speaking today, he said: "We're working in good faith to try and resolve this issue. And yes, I really would like to see that apology issued this year." The Tánaiste said there have been "a number of areas where progress has been made". However, he added: "What we're endeavouring to do here is to resolve all the outstanding issues. The view was always to try and resolve the outstanding issues and then have the apology."
